mechanism: Estradiol increases thromboembolic risk through prothrombotic effects on coagulation factors while enoxaparin provides anticoagulation, creating opposing pharmacodynamic effects and increased bleeding risk with concurrent use.
action: Monitor closely for signs of thromboembolism or bleeding; consider alternative contraception or evaluate continued necessity of anticoagulation; assess individual risk-benefit ratio given competing prothrombotic and anticoagulant effects.
